header.name: Brewery_V0
header.full_name: Brewery V0: beer production, spent grains sold as animal feed
header.authors_and_contributors: Pullah Bhatnagar, Daniel Flórez-Orrego, Oktay Boztas, Meire Ribeiro Domingos, François Maréchal, EPFL IPESE research group
header.description: Brewery that converts malt, corn and water into bottled beer: mashing, lautering, wort boiling, whirlpool and wort cooling, fermentation and maturation, chillage and filtration, dilution and pasteurisation, cleaning in place and bottle washing; the spent grains are sold as animal feed. 27 thermal streams per 1 t/h of beer.
header.main_related_publication: Bhatnagar, P., Flórez-Orrego, D., Boztas, O., Ribeiro Domingos, M., Margni, M., Maréchal, F., Decarbonizing breweries and distilleries through integrated process and energy system optimization. Manuscript, EPFL IPESE

units.unit_description: This unit converts malt, corn and water into 1 t/h of bottled beer: mashing, lautering, wort boiling, whirlpool and wort cooling, fermentation and maturation, chillage and filtration, dilution and pasteurisation, cleaning in place and the washing of returnable bottles. The spent grains leave the site as animal feed. In the OSMOSE model, the heat streams are grouped by section into the units Mashing, Lautering, Wort_boiling, Whirlpool, CIP, Beer_treatment, Bottle_washing, Wort_cooling, Fermentation, Maturation and Chillage, and the material flows and the electricity into the unit Plant_boundary, all at the scale CAPACITY.

unit_info.full_name: Brewery, spent grains to animal feed

units.connectors_description: The unit takes malt, corn (adjunct), water for mashing, sparge water, whirlpool make-up water, dilution water, water for cleaning (CIP), caustic soda (NaOH) and water for bottle washing, and electricity, and delivers beer, spent grains (dregs), vapour from wort boiling, trub, CO2 from fermentation, hot water to cleaning and bottle-washing wastewater. The material flows close at 1,972.4 kg/h in and out.

units.heat_streams_description: 16 cold and 11 hot streams per 1 t/h of beer, from the brewery study of Maréchal et al. (2013), the same plant as the brewery model simulated in DWSIM by Bhatnagar, Flórez-Orrego and Boztas (Bhatnagar et al., manuscript). Phase changes and the heat released at constant temperature in fermentation, maturation and chillage have a span of 0.1 K; the ΔTmin/2 contribution is 5 K, and 2 K for the boiling of the wort and the condensation of its vapour. Fermentation, maturation and chilling are refrigeration demands at the beer temperature.
